clue.text: Braid makes the round in eight pints

indicators.note: in tells us the round thing is placed inside the measure of eight pints

parts.note: a gallon is eight pints
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A drinker's tally of rounds amounting to eight pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O, the round, inside GALLON, the eight-pint measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A galloon is a narrow ornamental trimming or lace used to edge clothes, so it is a kind of braid.

clue.text: Film undertaker in church

definitions.meaning: one who undertakes vows for a child at a baptism

explanation.surface: A funeral director appearing in a church scene of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaker' suggests a funeral director; here it is one who undertakes promises as sponsor at a christening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godfather is the famous Coppola film, and a male baptismal sponsor makes promises for the child.

clue.text: Trojan priest's fuel return has nothing added

indicators.note: return says the fuel's name is read in reverse

parts.note: coal is a fuel
nothing is zero, the letter O
on means added, as in tacked on

explanation.surface: A Trojan priest's fuel coming back with nothing extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns COAL into LAOC; then O (nothing) and ON (added).
explanation.definitionFit: Laocoon was the priest of Troy who warned against the wooden horse and was killed by sea serpents.

clue.text: Tricky way to open Parliament after a purge

definitions.note: the definition is a way of winning tricks, taken as the card-play action

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
the Rump Parliament was what remained after Pride's Purge of 1648

explanation.surface: A cunning route to opening a purged Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge or whist, to overtrump is to play a higher trump than one already played, a way to take a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a higher trump to beat another player's trump is a means of winning a trick at cards.

clue.text: Steal, and you'll finish up in this, my lad

definitions.text: you'll finish up in this, my lad
definitions.meaning: a warning that a thief ends in prison or a police station

explanation.surface: A stern warning to a boy that stealing leads to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'nick' means both to steal and a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses one short word both for pinching goods and for the jail a thief ends up in.

clue.text: Master jumps for joy ?

definitions.meaning: the captain of a ship, its master
one who skips about in delight

explanation.surface: A captain leaping about in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain is its skipper, and someone who skips with glee is literally a skipper too.

clue.text: 20 for instance, a gullible one for this stuff

parts.note: the answer to 20 across is a prophetess, an example of a seer
a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A prophetess and a dupe both drawn to some material.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is SIBYL, a prophetess, so an example of a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered striped cotton fabric, so it is a kind of cloth or stuff.

clue.text: Accustom one lot of railwaymen to take note

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Getting a railway worker used to taking notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was the British National Union of Railwaymen. The page prints (6), but the light has five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to harden or habituate them to something unpleasant.

clue.text: Bard's lost girl

parts.note: Shakespeare's heroine of The Winter's Tale, abandoned as a baby, whose name means lost in Latin

explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare. In The Winter's Tale the baby princess is abandoned and named for being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita, Latin for the lost one, is the abandoned daughter of Leontes in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Wordsworth's mount upset Mrs Lord-right ?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: a lord's wife is a lady

explanation.surface: Wordsworth's horse upsetting a titled lady, who claims she is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LADY R over. Rydal Mount, in the Lake District, was Wordsworth's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Mount in the Lake District was the poet's home from 1813, so this is the name of his mount.

clue.text: Faineant clubman Wooster

definitions.meaning: Bertie Wooster, P G Wodehouse's hero

explanation.surface: Bertie Wooster described as an idler and a man about his club.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is the idle young gentleman of P G Wodehouse's comic novels; his London club is the Drones.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer living off others is called a drone after the male bee, and members of Wodehouse's Drones Club share the name.

clue.text: Money order-state of indebtedness — what a career!

definitions.note: the definition is an exclamation describing a career, taken as the adjective in a phrase about an up-and-down career

parts.note: a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money
being in the red means owing money

explanation.surface: Someone's financial history of payments and debts as a turbulent career.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'chequered career': a career full of ups and downs.
explanation.definitionFit: A career with many changes of fortune, good and bad, is called a chequered one.

clue.text: Toe trouble in a sloth-that is a rodent

indicators.note: in places the toe complaint inside the sloth's name

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth of South America
gout is a painful inflammation that typically attacks the big toe

explanation.surface: An animal with sore feet: a sloth with gout.
explanation.walkthrough: AI is a crossword favourite: a three-toed sloth. 'in' puts GOUT inside it; 'that is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a long-legged burrowing rodent of Central and South America.

clue.text: Strange perception by Alice perhaps in particular

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, an uncanny sixth sense

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the name could be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Alice in Wonderland having strange perceptions, in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALICE to ECIAL, which follows ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is an older synonym of special, meaning particular or exceptional.

clue.text: Gaelic Scotch

parts.note: the old Gaelic name for whisky, meaning water of life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' here is whisky, not the people; the Gaelic phrase for water of life gave English the word whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Usquebaugh is the Gaelic term for whisky, from uisge beatha, water of life.

clue.text: Farm-worker to high-class Indian

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
U means upper-class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A farm labourer addressing a high-caste Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND is an old Scots and northern English word for a skilled farm hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, the majority religion of India.

clue.text: Ascot as modified in such an American course

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged racecourse goes inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: modified says the letters of Ascot are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Ascot racecourse remodelled on an American course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' turns ASCOT into COTAS, and 'in' sets that inside SUCH, between SUC and H. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Succotash is a North American side dish of sweetcorn and lima beans, so it is a course in a meal.

clue.text: Old boy sees about French relative's last rites

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: about means the word for sees goes round the French word

parts.note: taken as written
qui is the French relative pronoun meaning who

explanation.surface: A former pupil looking into a French relation's funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relative' suggests family, but it is a relative pronoun: French QUI, which 'about' puts inside SEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequies are funeral rites, the ceremonies at a burial.

clue.text: Flower with bell about to ring in here

indicators.note: in places the mixed-up pieces inside the word here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of bell are turned around into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bell-shaped flower about to be rung in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BELL to LLEB; add O (ring), and 'in' puts LLEBO inside HERE, between HE and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebores, such as the Christmas rose, are winter-flowering plants with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Car with repute, after repair, can win again

indicators.note: after repair means the pieces have been fixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A car with a good reputation, once repaired, can win races again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after repair' rearranges CAR and REPUTE together; 'can' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture something, such as a title, is to take or win it back.

clue.text: Room for commercials, or music

parts.note: a word for a room that also names a body of merchants and a kind of small-ensemble music

explanation.walkthrough: 'commercials' suggests adverts; it means traders, as in a chamber of commerce. Chamber music is for small groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, a chamber of commerce is a traders' association, and chamber music is for small ensembles.

clue.text: Bookseller is backed by money

indicators.note: backed means the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bookseller who is supported financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns IS into SI. The Cumaean Sibyl offered nine books of prophecy to King Tarquin of Rome, which makes her a bookseller.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend tells of the Sibyl selling her prophetic books to Tarquin, so a prophetess of that line was literally a bookseller.

clue.text: Harris's brother holds pointed tool-quarrelsome type

indicators.note: holds means the first word wraps round the tool

parts.note: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus stories of Brer Rabbit and Brer Fox; Brer means brother
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Harris's brother holding a sharp tool, a quarrelsome sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris is Joel Chandler Harris, whose Uncle Remus tales use BRER (brother) as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawler is someone who gets into noisy fights, a pugnacious type.

clue.text: Help sent back by native community with bitter criticism

indicators.note: sent back means the word for help is written in reverse

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a native community

explanation.surface: Aid returned by an indigenous group with harsh words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, abusive verbal attack.

clue.text: Adjust line of 25

definitions.meaning: to straighten a rank of soldiers
the answer to 25 down means clothing

explanation.surface: Straightening a row of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress ranks by lining up straight. 25 down is GEAR, meaning clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops dress a line by aligning it, and clothing is also called dress.

clue.text: Perhaps a sort of joint

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could stand in another order

explanation.surface: A tentative description of some kind of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges A SORT; 'of' is a link. 'Joint' is meat, not a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: Old-fashioned? It's as broad as it's long

definitions.meaning: conventional and out of date, a fuddy-duddy

definitions.text: It's as broad as it's long
definitions.meaning: describes a shape whose width equals its length

explanation.surface: A dated phrase about something that makes no difference either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull conventional person is called a square, and a square shape has equal sides.

clue.text: 22 dn in a box for Carmen'?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 22 down means clothes
read as car men, the drivers' gearbox

explanation.surface: Costume kept in a box for the opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' suggests Bizet's opera, where dress would be costume; split it as car men, whose gearbox houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means clothing, and the gear wheels sit in a car's gearbox.

clue.text: Castle opening, distributing Sarum Beer

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A castle doorway handing out local Salisbury beer.
explanation.walkthrough: SARUM is the old name of Salisbury. 'distributing' rearranges SARUM BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasure is an opening in a castle wall or battlement for firing through.

clue.text: Primitive dwelling has one grand mod, con.

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a modern convenience, here a toilet, is a loo

explanation.surface: A primitive hut boasting a modern convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mod. con.' is a modern convenience in British estate-agent speak; LOO is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit snow house, a simple shelter.

clue.text: Time inside seems elastic

definitions.meaning: to give or extend like a rubber band

explanation.surface: A prison sentence feels as if it goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term is slang a stretch, and material that gives when pulled will stretch.

clue.text: Twelfth man's reticence

definitions.meaning: in cricket the substitute fielder, an extra player

explanation.surface: A cricket substitute who keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the extra player who fields for an injured team-mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket substitute is the reserve, and a reticent manner is also called reserve.
